summary: Every Dreamer prompt now says where the doctrine ends and the objective begins.
details: The doctrine and the objective are each wrapped in a named tag rather than joined by a bare newline, so the system prompt has the same structure the adaptor's input has always had.
Each run's instruction digest is taken over the served text rather than the two bodies, so renaming a document moves the digest the way editing one does.
limitations: No measurement accompanies this. The prompt bytes change for all six adaptors and none of them has a paired A/B suite; culture and note-curation have no eval suite at all.
